questions.text:
Consider the following relation

Cinema(theater, address, capacity)

Which of the following options will be needed at the end of the SQL query

SELECT P1.address FROM Cinema P1

such that it always finds the addresses of theaters with maximum capacity?
questions.solution:
A theater has maximum capacity when its capacity is [latex]\ge[/latex] every capacity in the table, i.e. [latex]\ge[/latex] ALL.

[latex]\ge[/latex] ANY returns every theater. [latex]\gt[/latex] ALL (max) / [latex]\gt[/latex] ANY (max) returns nothing.

Answer: WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\ge[/latex] All (select P2.capacity from Cinema P2)

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\geq[/latex] All (select P2.capacity from Cinema P2)
WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\geq[/latex] Any (select P2.capacity from Cinema P2)
WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\gt[/latex] All (select max(P2.capacity) from Cinema P2)
WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\gt[/latex] Any (select max(P2.capacity) from Cinema P2)

questions.text:
Consider the relation X(P,Q,R,S,T,U) with the following set of functional dependencies
F= {{P,R}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{S,T}, {P,S,U}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{Q,R} }
Which of the following is the trivial functional dependency in [latex]F^{+}[/latex], where [latex]F^{+}[/latex] is closure of F ?
questions.solution:
A dependency is trivial when its right side is a subset of its left side.

{S} [latex]\subseteq[/latex] {P, S}, so {P, S} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {S} is trivial. In option 2, T is not in {P, R}.

Answer: {P, S} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {S}

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: {P,R}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{S,T}
{P,R}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{R,T}
{P,S}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{S}
{P,S,U}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{Q}

questions.text: Consider two relations R1(A,B) with the tuples (1,5), (3,7) and R2(A,C) = (1,7), (4,9). Assume that R(A,B,C) is the full natural outer join of R1 and R2. Consider the following tuples of the form (A,B,C): a = (1,5,null), b = (1,null,7), c = (3, null, 9), d = (4,7,null), e = (1,5,7), f = (3,7,null), g = (4,null,9). Which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.solution:
Natural join on A:
- A = 1 matches: (1, 5, 7) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] e
- R1 (3, 7) has no match: (3, 7, null) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f
- R2 (4, 9) has no match: (4, null, 9) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] g

Since A = 1 matched, (1, 5, null) and (1, null, 7) do not appear.

Answer: R contains e, f, g but not a, b

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: R contains a, b, e, f, g but not c, d.
R contains all of a, b, c, d, e, f, g.
R contains e, f, g but not a, b.
R contains e but not f, g.

questions.text:
Consider a simple checkpointing protocol and the following set of operations in the log.
(start, T4); (write, T4, y, 2, 3); (start, T1); (commit, T4); (write, T1, z, 5, 7);
(checkpoint);
(start, T2); (write, T2, x, 1, 9); (commit, T2); (start, T3), (write, T3, z, 7, 2);
If a crash happens now and the system tries to recover using both undo and redo operations, what are the contents of the undo list and the redo list?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- T4 committed before the checkpoint [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] already safe, nothing to do.
- T1 started before the checkpoint and never committed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undo.
- T2 committed after the checkpoint [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] redo.
- T3 never committed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undo.

Answer: Undo: T3, T1; Redo: T2

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Undo: T3, T1; Redo: T2
Undo: T3, T1; Redo: T2, T4
Undo: none; Redo: T2, T4, T3, T1
Undo: T3, T1, T4; Redo: T2

questions.text:
Consider the following transaction involving two bank accounts x and y.

read(x); x:=x-50; write(x); read(y); y:=y+50; write(y)

The constraint that the sum of the accounts x and y should remain constant is that of
questions.solution:
Keeping x + y constant is an integrity rule of the database, which the transaction must preserve. That is the consistency property.

Answer: Consistency

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Consistency
Isolation
Durability
